clue.text: Harder to get jokes about renouncing king and queen

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, as in about-face, so the letters run the other way
to renounce something is to give it up, so a letter is surrendered from the word

parts.note: cracks are wisecracks, quips
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard crossword queen

explanation.surface: A comedian finds laughs harder to come by once the royal jokes are off limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Renouncing' applies only to the king; the queen is added afterwards rather than removed. Jokes in the sense of wisecracks supply the base word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarcer is in shorter supply, so it is comparatively more difficult to obtain.

clue.text: Parties regularly taking Scotch in a glass

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth letters and so on of these words

explanation.surface: Party-goers who make a habit of having a whisky in a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: The drink is pure surface: the letters come from the odd positions of the last four words.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal gathering or get-together, so socials are simply parties.

clue.text: For the most part, Texas city's revolutionary paper is absolutely fantastic?

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so these letters are read backwards
most but not all of the word is used, so its final letter goes

parts.note: Dallas is a major city in Texas
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A Dallas newspaper with radical views is praised as absolutely brilliant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' in the surface means wonderful, but in the definition it means belonging to fantasy; the question mark flags that shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that was all a dream existed only in the imagination, which is the literal sense of fantastic.

clue.text: Overthrow towards slip

parts.note: a coup is the overthrow of a government
on as in moving on, towards a place

explanation.walkthrough: 'Overthrow' and 'slip' both sound like verbs of falling; only the last word is the definition, and it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon is a small printed piece of paper exchanged for a discount, a paper slip.

clue.text: Associated masseurs did this?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: mixed socially with other people

definitions.note: a cryptic second meaning, taken literally
definitions.meaning: second meaning, taken literally: what massage therapists do to the upper back

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the literal reading of an idiom: masseurs really do knead people's upper backs.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub shoulders with people is an idiom for mixing or spending time with them socially.

clue.text: Read South American country's leading journalist

parts.note: Peru with its possessive S
the editor, abbreviated ED, is the leading figure on a newspaper

explanation.surface: A reader looking through the work of the top reporter in a South American country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read' is past tense here, pronounced red, matching the -ED ending.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to examine or look through writing, so perused works as a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: I help orphans set it up — without any English benefactors

indicators.note: to set something up is to arrange it anew, so these letters are reordered
without any means lacking every instance, so all copies of a letter are removed

parts.note: the letters as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A charity worker vows to help orphans get established, with no English donors involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set it' does double duty: it is fodder, while 'set it up' reads as the arrangement signal. Both Es go before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Philanthropists are wealthy people who give money to good causes, the classic benefactors.

clue.text: Wine, beer and intially rum too — this means one's expecting the worst

definitions.text: this means one's expecting the worst

parts.note: red is a kind of wine
ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: initially points to the beginnings of the following words, so only their opening letters count

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone who has had wine, beer and rum as well is bracing for a terrible hangover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intially' is a misprint for initially in the printed clue. The drinks list reads as a binge, but each drink supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A red alert is the highest state of warning, declared when danger or disaster is imminent.

clue.text: That woman on medical TV show is thin

parts.note: she is the pronoun for that woman
ER is the American hospital drama series

explanation.surface: An actress on a hospital drama turns out to be skinny.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical TV show is the long-running American hospital drama set in a Chicago emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer fabric such as fine stockings is very fine and see-through, meaning thin.

clue.text: Dismount in cycling arena in outskirts of Dortmund

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it
cycling means going round in a loop, so a letter moves from one end of the word to the other
the outskirts are the edges, so only the outer letters are used

parts.note: the first and last letters
a scene is an arena of activity, as in the political scene

explanation.surface: A cyclist gets off their bike inside a velodrome on the edge of a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' looks like part of the velodrome picture, but it tells you to move the last E of SCENE round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismount is to come down from a horse or bike, so descend is a close verb synonym.

clue.text: Conservative nun is shocked with bordello's lack of discrimination

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: shocked implies being thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the possessive S included

explanation.surface: A prim nun is appalled at how indiscriminate a brothel's clientele is.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on discrimination: in the surface it means choosiness, in the answer the ability to tell colours apart. A bordello is a brothel.
explanation.definitionFit: Colour blindness is an inability to distinguish certain colours, literally failing to discriminate between hues.

clue.text: Stars in animated Dan Dare securing award

definitions.note: plural where the answer names one constellation

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece holds another
animated means lively and moving about, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written
the OM, Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: Stars appearing in an animated version of the Dan Dare space comic, which wins a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan Dare is a British comic-strip space pilot, so stars fit the scene. OM stands for the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a northern constellation, a named group of stars in the night sky.

clue.text: Great section seen when Brazil and Argentina meet

indicators.note: things that meet are brought up against each other, so the pieces are joined end to end
a section is only part of something, so just some letters are used

parts.note: the final letter, at the join
its opening four letters, the stretch just after the join

explanation.surface: A football pundit promises a great passage of play whenever these two South American rivals face each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Write the two country names side by side with no gap; the answer is the stretch of letters that straddles the point where they touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Large and great are ordinary adjectives meaning big in size.

clue.text: Ooze goes backwards

indicators.note: backwards means in the opposite direction, so the letters read right to left

parts.note: to go is an informal way of saying to urinate, which is to pee

explanation.surface: Sludge that flows the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes' looks like the verb of movement, but here it means relieves oneself, as in needing to go.
explanation.definitionFit: To ooze is to leak out slowly through something, which is exactly what seeping liquid does.

clue.text: Ridiculed artist almost dies at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and disoriented, so these letters are mixed up
almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mocked painter nearly perishes on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' belongs to the tragic story, but it is the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To satirise someone is to mock them with humour and exaggeration, so satirised means mocked.

clue.text: Second home after boat — an artist might rough it here

definitions.text: an artist might rough it here

indicators.note: after means following, so one piece is written behind another

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
a pad is slang for someone's flat or home

explanation.surface: A painter keeps a holiday home as well as a boat, and roughs it on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough it' suggests camping out, but here to rough something is to draw a rough outline of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch pad is a drawing block where artists make rough preliminary drawings, their roughs.

clue.text: LAX-O'Hare's terminal for sport

parts.note: the airport code splits as LA, Los Angeles, plus X, which is the shape of a cross

indicators.note: a terminal is an end point, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: An airport-to-airport link: LAX in Los Angeles, O'Hare in Chicago, and their terminal buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: LAX and O'Hare are real airports, so 'terminal' looks like a building; it is the last letter, and LAX splits into LA plus X.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team game played with netted sticks, a sport of North American origin.

clue.text: Circuitous route — intend to replace train's first carriage

indicators.note: replacing means swapping one thing out and putting another in its place

parts.note: a detour is a roundabout way to a place
to mean to do something is to intend it

indicators.note: first means the opening one, so only the initial letter counts

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A rail diversion where the plan is to swap out the train's leading coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' is the railway word in the surface, but the definition is carriage in the sense of how a person holds themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage can mean posture and bearing, and demeanour is outward manner and behaviour.

clue.text: Spoiled old man hiding say, a million in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters run backwards
to hide something is to keep it inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: old man is slang for father, dad
EG, for example, is what say means
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A spoilt elderly father secretly squirrels away a million for his retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoiled' is the definition, not a description of the old man; 'say' is the usual shorthand for for example.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spoiled has been harmed or ruined, so damaged is a direct adjective synonym.

clue.text: Line to appear on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so we go by the spoken sound of a word

parts.note: to seem is to appear to be

explanation.surface: An actor's line that gets to be heard on a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' reads as a script line; it is the stitched line joining two pieces of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A seam is the line where two pieces of fabric are sewn together, or a thin geological layer.

clue.text: Spooner's delivering savvy Bluth's hot ticket

indicators.note: the Oxford don famous for trading the opening sounds of neighbouring words is the one speaking

parts.note: to have sussed something is to be savvy about it; handed the M from the next word, this sound results
the setter Bluth is me; taking the S sound, this word results

explanation.surface: The setter's knowing pick for the show everyone wants tickets to.
explanation.walkthrough: Suss is British slang for shrewdness or working something out, and the setter refers to themself by name, so Bluth is me. Swap the opening sounds of suss me.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot ticket is an event everyone wants to attend, which is what a must-see show is.

clue.text: Inflexible, adult bones

parts.note: stern means strict and unbending
A is the film classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up's stiff skeleton.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits the charade from the definition; STERNA is the Latin plural of sternum.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone, so sterna are several of these flat chest bones.

clue.text: Starter for Ted Heath's touring car

indicators.note: touring means going around, so one piece travels round another

parts.note: a heath is open uncultivated land, a moor

indicators.note: a starter is the opening course, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: Former UK prime minister Ted Heath gets his touring car going.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath was a British prime minister of the 1970s, so the name reads as one person; split it into the initial and the moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor is an informal, somewhat old-fashioned British word for a motor car.

clue.text: Disagreements when all 7 characters take one step to the right

indicators.text: take one step to the right
indicators.note: moving one step along the alphabet swaps each letter for its successor

parts.note: the letters of the answer to 7 down

explanation.surface: Squabbles break out when the whole cast of seven has to move one place across the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Each letter of SHEER moves one place on in the alphabet: S to T, H to I, E to F, E to F, R to S.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a minor quarrel, so tiffs are petty disagreements or squabbles.

clue.text: Slap possibly leaving small marks on cheek

definitions.note: an example of slap, and the answer is plural

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed on means added after, so one piece follows another

parts.note: lip is insolence, cheek
S is the abbreviation for small
ticks are marks made on a checklist

explanation.surface: A slap in the face leaves little red marks on the cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: Slap is British slang for make-up, not a blow; and cheek is impudence, lip, not the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipstick is one kind of make-up, so lipsticks are an example of what the slang word covers.

clue.text: Way to enhance car in first gear — stop jumping the lights, finally

indicators.note: jumping suggests things leaping about out of place, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the ends of words, so their last letters are kept

parts.note: the last letters of each word

explanation.surface: Driving advice: pull away in first gear and stop running red lights.
explanation.walkthrough: The driving-lesson surface hides fodder: 'first gear stop' is scrambled with the final letters of 'the lights'. Go-faster stripes are decorative stripes painted on cars, a British phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Go-faster stripes are painted decoration meant to make a car look sporty, a cosmetic way to jazz one up.

clue.text: Gets rid of detective books after relinquishing advance

indicators.note: after means following, so one piece comes behind another

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: to relinquish is to give something up, so letters are dropped

parts.note: the Gospels are the four books of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John
to go is to move forward, advance

explanation.surface: A reader clears out their crime novels after giving back the publisher's advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books' suggests novels and 'advance' an author's payment, but the books are biblical and the advance is a verb meaning go.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel fears or doubts is to drive them away, making them disappear entirely.

clue.text: Bandage covering wife's cut

indicators.note: to cover something is to go around it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a saddle of lamb or venison is a joint of meat, a butcher's cut
W is the abbreviation for wife, as in marriage records

explanation.surface: A dressing is wrapped over the wound on the wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' reads as a wound needing dressing, but it is a joint of meat; the 's after wife is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To swaddle is to wrap tightly in cloth, which is what one does when binding with a bandage.
